sentences.text: Shri Ravinandan Dwivedi, learned counsel for the applic  Shri Y.D. Yadav, learned Government Adv  respondent/State.

This is first application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.176/2023 dated 15.04.2023 registered at Police Station Chhipawada, District Harda (M.P.) for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 366,
376(3), 376(2)(n) of IPC and Section 5/6 of the POCSO Act, 2012.
Learned counsel for applicant has submitted that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the crime in question.
The applicant is in custody since 29.01.2024 and trial will take considerable time to conclude.
He further submits that applicant is permanent resident of district and there is no likelihood of his absconding from the clutches of law or tampering with prosecution evidence.
He also submits that the applicant is ready to furnish adequate surety and shall abide by all the directions and conditions which may be imposed by this Court.
Upon these grounds, the applicant may be released on bail.
Learned counsel for the State has opposed the bail application and prayed for its rejection.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case-diary.

This bail application has been argued on the ground that a child has been born to the prosecutrix and to provide proper care and protection to the 2 MCRC-22425-2024 prosecutrix and the child, the applicant should be released on bail.
Learned counsel for the State has opposed the bail application on the ground that the prosecutrix was below 16 years of age at the time of incident and she was subjected to sexual abuse.
Taking these facts into consideration, this bail application is dismissed.

(ANURADHA SHUKLA) JUDGE sjk Umesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125391524/
